thread:
samir: seeing a spike in GPU allocation failures in us-west1. pods are pending and CA isn't creating new gpu nodes.
maya: any errors in the autoscaler logs? did it hit quota or couldn't find matching instance type?
samir: infra-bot posted this: ERROR: failed to create instance: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for zone us-west1-b. (code=403)
chao: yep quota. we have regional quota but zonal availability is patchy — some zones report NO_CAPACITY_AVAILABLE. :grimacing:
maya: are we using zonal node pools for gpu workloads or regional? I remember a few pools are zonal to control costs.
samir: currently zonal for lower latency to storage. node pools: gpu-west-a (zonal), gpu-west-b (zonal), gpu-regional-fallback (regional, smaller capacity).
chao: cluster-autoscaler usually prefers same-zone node groups. if zone is out of capacity it might not try other zones unless configured.
maya: config we use has: --balance-similar-node-groups=true and --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false. maybe we need to enable cross-zone scale-up behavior.
chao: two levers: 1) let CA scale across nodegroups (regional), 2) fallback reroute traffic to a dedicated regional cluster using our smart-routing policy.
oncall-sre: routing fallback exists but sharding + model pinning makes it complicated for in-flight sessions. fallback would increase latency and cost.
samir: infra-bot also shows GCP capacity errors: "ZONE_AVAILABILITY_ISSUE: There are no valid zones for your request" in us-west1-b.
maya: short-term: increase GPU quota for us-west region and enable CA flags to allow cross-group balancing. medium-term: add a small reserved pool of 2-4 guaranteed GPUs in another region as hot-standby.
chao: also consider tainting reserved-hot nodes with: node.kubernetes.io/role=fallback:NoSchedule and use pod tolerations only when primary can't schedule. reduces accidental usage and cost.
oncall-sre: cost question — fallback regional GPUs are ~1.4x more expensive due to egress and inter-region network. fine for failover but not for steady traffic.
maya: patch suggestion for autoscaler: set --expendable-pods-priority-cutoff to move best-effort to preemptible pools and allow guaranteed pods to trigger reserved pool.
samir: here's a quick command to inspect pool sizes and autoscaler status:

```
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool -o wide
kubectl describe clusterautoscaler
``` 

maya: I'll open a quota request with cloud console for us-west region now and add an alert if any zone reports NO_CAPACITY_AVAILABLE.
chao: I'll prototype a small NodePool + taint + toleration approach and a simple routing rule that fails over to regional cluster with a 100ms added latency threshold.
oncall-sre: create a runbook entry for this failover path and mark who owns the reserved pool. I'll add an oncall playbook step.
infra-bot: alert created: Quota increase request submitted for project:redwood-prod, region:us-west1 (request id: rq-2026-03-18-42).
samir: thanks — follow-ups: maya (quota), chao (fallback nodepool PR), oncall-sre (runbook). I'll monitor for the next 2 hours.
maya: noted. :thumbsup:
chao: will post PR link when ready.
oncall-sre: I'll add a temporary dashboard showing zonal GPU availability and autoscaler decisions.
samir: good plan. tagging @maya @chao @oncall-sre. any objections? :thinking:
maya: none. go ahead.
